rules.title: Sunday, 2nd and 4th Saturdays, and listed holidays are closed
rules.statement: A date is not a business day when extract(dow) is 0 (Sunday), when it is a Saturday (dow 6) and ceil(day of month / 7) is 2 or 4, or when lms.holiday has that date with state_code ALL or the state passed in. Every other date is a business day. A 1st, 3rd or 5th Saturday is a business day unless it is also a listed holiday, and a holiday for a different state does not count.
rules.notes: Saturday bands are days 8-14 (2nd) and 22-28 (4th). Days 29-31 are the 5th band.

rules.title: Next business day moves forward at most ten days
rules.statement: If the date is already a business day, it is returned unchanged. Otherwise it moves forward one calendar day at a time until the date is a business day or 10 steps have been taken. If it is still not a business day, that last date is returned anyway.
rules.notes: The header at lines 40-41 describes the same stop after 10 steps.

rules.title: A FIXED loan uses its fixed rate with no rounding
rules.statement: When rate_type is exactly FIXED, the rate for the day is fixed_rate_pct. The value is not rounded. A null fixed_rate_pct is returned as null, not replaced with zero or a benchmark.
rules.notes: The loan row is read at line 75. This function does not raise an error when the loan is missing.

rules.title: A non-fixed rate is stepped back to a reset date
rules.statement: When rate_type is not exactly FIXED, whole months from disb_date to the day are extract(year from age) times 12 plus extract(month from age). The day part of age is ignored. Integer division then drops the remainder so the month count is a multiple of reset_months, and the reset date is disb_date plus that many months. There is no explicit FLOATING test.
rules.notes: A null or zero reset_months is not handled. A null rate_type takes this path rather than the fixed-rate return.

rules.title: No benchmark on the reset date falls back to the fixed rate
rules.statement: The benchmark is the lms.benchmark_rate row for the loan's benchmark_code with the latest effective_date on or before the reset date. When a row is found, the rate is that rate_pct plus the spread, and a null spread is treated as 0. When no row is found, the function returns fixed_rate_pct and does not add the spread. Neither result is rounded.
rules.notes: The lookup orders by effective_date descending only, with no tie-break when two rows share a date.

rules.title: Receipts pay the oldest open installment, interest then principal
rules.statement: fn_apply_to_installments applies an amount to installment rows for the loan whose interest_due is not null and which still have unpaid interest or unpaid principal, in ascending inst_no. On each installment it pays unpaid interest first and unpaid principal second, and only a positive slice is applied. It adds that slice to paid_interest or paid_principal, and returns the amount left, the interest paid and the principal paid. It does not round, and it does not update the loan row. A null amount is not treated as zero.
rules.notes: sp_prepayment_quote does not call this function. A null paid_interest or paid_principal makes that slice null, so the slice is skipped.

rules.title: A ledger post is one insert of the values supplied
rules.statement: sp_post_ledger inserts one lms.loan_ledger row with the loan, date, entry type, amount and note it is given. It does not round the amount, reject a null, or update the loan.

rules.title: A quote is refused when the loan, status, date or product is not eligible
rules.statement: The quote raises LMS-001 when the loan id does not exist, LMS-021 when status is not exactly ACTIVE, and LMS-002 when the quote date is strictly before the disbursement date. A quote on the disbursement date is allowed. It raises LMS-003 when the loan's product_code is not in lms.loan_product. There is no exception handler, so any of these stops the function before a QUOTE ledger row is written.
rules.notes: A null quote date does not satisfy the before-disbursement test, so LMS-002 is not raised for null.

rules.title: Quoted principal falls back to the amount disbursed
rules.statement: The principal in the quote is principal_outstanding. When that is null, the quote uses principal_disbursed. The value is not rounded.

rules.title: Quoted interest is stored accrual plus simple interest for actual days
rules.statement: New interest runs from last_run_date, or from the disbursement date when last_run_date is null, to the quote date. Days are the actual calendar difference, and a negative difference is replaced with 0. The year divisor is 365 when day_count is exactly ACT365 and 360 for every other value, including null. The rate for the quote date alone is applied to the whole period: principal times rate / 100 times days / year basis. That new amount is rounded to 2 decimal places and then added to accrued_interest. accrued_interest is not rounded, and a null accrued_interest makes the quoted interest null.
rules.notes: round(numeric, 2) rounds halves away from zero. The sum with accrued_interest is not rounded again. The comment on line 221 does not mention the stored accrual.

rules.title: A quote copies penal interest and does not accrue more
rules.statement: Quoted penal interest is accrued_penal, copied as stored. The quote calculates no new penal interest and does not replace a null with zero.
rules.notes: The comment on line 228 matches this: already accrued penal stays, and nothing new is added.

rules.title: Outstanding fees are copied into the quote
rules.statement: Quoted fees are fees_outstanding, with no rounding and no substitution when the value is null.

rules.title: Fixed-rate prepayment fee is waived unless more than three months remain
rules.statement: The prepayment fee starts at 0. It is charged only when rate_type is exactly FIXED, prepay_fee_pct is not null, and whole months of tenor left are greater than 3. Elapsed months are the year and month parts of age from disbursement to the quote date, so leftover days are ignored. Months left are tenor_months minus those elapsed months. The fee is the quoted principal times prepay_fee_pct / 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. A rate that is not FIXED, a null fee percent, or 3 or fewer months left, including a negative remainder, leaves the fee at 0.
rules.notes: The header at line 173 says the fee is waived in the last 3 months. The charge test is months left greater than 3, so exactly 3 is waived.

rules.title: GST is 18 percent of the prepayment fee plus outstanding fees
rules.statement: GST is the prepayment fee plus fees outstanding, times c_gst_rate / 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. c_gst_rate is the numeric constant 18, declared with no precision or scale. Principal, interest and penal interest are not in the GST base. A null fees outstanding makes GST null. The prepayment fee itself is never null, because it is set to 0 first.
rules.notes: The constant is declared at line 193 as c_gst_rate constant numeric := 18.

rules.title: The payoff total subtracts the advance and cannot go below zero
rules.statement: The total is principal plus interest plus penal plus fees plus the prepayment fee plus GST, minus advance_balance. There is no further rounding. When the total is less than 0 it is set to 0. When any of those amounts is null the total is null, and a null total is not replaced with 0 because the floor test is only less than zero. The advance reduces the total only. The component outputs are left unchanged.
rules.notes: Line 245 says an advance balance reduces what the customer pays. It does not say the total is floored at zero.

rules.title: Valid-until is the next business day after the quote's business day
rules.statement: Valid-until is the next business day after the first business day on or after the quote date. Both steps use the loan's branch_state. When the quote date is itself a business day, valid-until is the following business day, so the quote date is the first of the two business days and valid-until is the second. The function does not store a time. Each step uses the helper that stops after 10 days, so a long run of non-working days can leave valid-until on a date that is not a business day.
rules.notes: The comment on line 252 says the quote is valid for two business days in the branch state.

rules.title: A successful quote posts one QUOTE row and does not change the loan
rules.statement: After the amounts are calculated, the function posts one ledger row of type QUOTE, dated the quote date, for the total, with the note 'valid until ' followed by the valid-until date. It does not update the loan, its balances or its installments, and it does not close the loan. The amount posted is that total, not a figure rounded again to 2 decimal places. If the valid-until date is null, the note is null.
rules.notes: Lines 176-177 say the function writes one QUOTE row and does not change the loan. In PostgreSQL, text joined to null with || is null.

contradictions.description: The header says the rate is the benchmark in force on the reset date plus the spread. When no benchmark row has an effective date on or before that reset date, the code returns fixed_rate_pct and does not add the spread.

The comment says this is interest since the last end-of-day run, rounded once at the end. The code sets quoted interest to the stored accrued_interest plus the new amount, and it rounds only the new amount to 2 decimal places.

open_questions: The year divisor is 365 only when day_count is exactly ACT365. Every other value, including null, uses 360, while the days are always the actual calendar difference. Confirm that this quote has no other day-count method.
New interest uses the single rate for the quote date across the whole period. A reset between the last run and the quote date does not split the days. Confirm that is intended.

accrued_interest, accrued_penal, fees_outstanding and advance_balance are not turned into zero when null. Any one of them being null makes the payoff total null, and the less-than-zero floor does not replace that null. Confirm nulls should not be treated as zero.

The prepayment fee is waived when whole months left are 3 or fewer, so exactly 3 is waived, and age() ignores leftover days. Confirm the waiver should start at exactly 3 whole months and ignore a partial month.

Valid-until is the next business day after the first business day on or after the quote date. A quote on a working Monday is valid through Tuesday, counting Monday as one of the two business days. Confirm the quote day counts.

Each business-day step stops after 10 calendar days and can return a non-working day. The quote uses that helper for valid-until. Confirm valid-until may fall on a non-working day after a long holiday.

The receipt helper pays by ascending inst_no, and only where interest_due is not null, with interest before principal on that installment before the next one. The quote never calls it. Confirm inst_no is oldest-first, and that a null interest_due means the installment is not billed.
If a non-fixed loan has no benchmark row on or before the reset date, the rate is fixed_rate_pct and no error is raised. Confirm that fallback is intended.
GST is 18% of the prepayment fee plus fees outstanding, rounded to 2 decimal places, and is not charged on principal, interest or penal. No comment describes GST. Confirm the base and the rate.

advance_balance is subtracted from the total only. The prepayment fee is still calculated on the full quoted principal, and the component outputs are not reduced to match the total. Confirm the fee base and the gross breakdown.

The header says to run the quote before end-of-day for the same date. The code does not check that. If last_run_date is already the quote date, the new day count is zero. Confirm quotes must be run before end-of-day.
The benchmark lookup orders by effective_date only. Two rows with the same effective_date have no further tie-break. Confirm which row should win.
Rate resets use whole months from disbursement and integer division by reset_months, so the day of the month does not move the reset date. Confirm resets should ignore the day.
The rate path tests only for the exact value FIXED. Every other rate_type, including null, uses the benchmark reset. Confirm that only a FLOATING loan should take that path.
